item.title: Curtis Flowers Has Died at 56. His Case Became a Symbol of Racial Bias.
item.description: A white district attorney tried Mr. Flowers six times for the same murder, always ensuring that few or no Black people were on the juries.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel
item.media:description: Curtis Flowers with his sister Priscilla Flowers-Ward exiting the Winston Choctaw Regional Correctional Facility in Louisville, Miss., on Dec. 16, 2019.

item.title: Wayne Lawson, Vanity Fair’s ‘Secret Weapon,’ Has Died
item.description: Working with Mr. Lawson, reporters said, was like taking a master class in writing: “He was a throwback to the old style of editing.”
item.dc:creator: Penelope Green

item.title: Cecily Gemmell, Winston Churchill’s Last Surviving Secretary, Has Died
item.description: Starting with the British leader at age 18, she traveled the world with him. “I was terrified of him,” she later recalled.
item.dc:creator: Barry Singer

item.title: Margaret Papandreou, American-Born First Lady of Greece, Dies at 102
item.description: The wife of Prime Minister Andreas Papandreou, she led reforms in the 1980s that helped legalize abortion and end other legal and social restrictions on women.
item.dc:creator: Brian Murphy
item.media:description: Margaret Papandreou in 1986. “The women’s movement is a political movement,” she once said. “It is a social revolution.”

item.title: Margaret Hamilton, Whose Software Guided the Apollo Missions, Has Died
item.description: Margaret Hamilton, the first female programmer hired to work on the space project at M.I.T., was 90.
item.dc:creator: Trip Gabriel
item.media:description: Margaret Hamilton with printed computer code in 1969.

item.title: Nana Patekar, Indian Actor Who Embodied the Everyman, Dies at 75
item.description: He brought the intensity of the stage to the screen and was praised for his craft and philanthropy. He was also accused of sexual harassment.
item.dc:creator: Lynsey Chutel and Pragati K.B.
item.media:description: Nana Patekar in 2023. He was a theater actor who brought intensity and coarse baritone to the screen.

item.title: Bill Harris Has Died. He Kidnapped Patty Hearst in 1974.
item.description: He was a disillusioned Vietnam veteran looking for purpose when he joined a revolutionary group known as the Symbionese Liberation Army.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:description: Bill Harris, center, after being captured in 1975, the year after the S.L.A. kidnapped Patty Hearst. Her family, he later said, “was in control of a media empire that we viewed as an arm of propaganda for the United States government.”

item.title: After Death of Bill Harris, a Look Back at the Symbionese Liberation Army
item.description: A small band of urban guerrillas, they hoped to topple the “ruling class” using guns and bombs. Instead, their efforts brought death and ruin.
item.dc:creator: Alex Williams
item.media:description: Six members of the S.L.A. died in a shootout with Los Angeles police in May 1974. Clockwise from top left, Camilla Hall, William Wolfe, Donald DeFreeze, Patricia Soltysik, Nancy Ling Perry and Angela Atwood.

item.title: Charles K. Williams II, Pioneering Archaeologist in Corinth, Has Died
item.description: Charles K. Williams II spent most of his career excavating sites in Corinth, including one where he found thousands of fragments of Roman frescoes.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: Before Computer Science Became a Boys’ Club, Margaret Hamilton Wrote the Code
item.description: The woman who helped put astronauts on the moon was a software engineer when the field was not prestigious or lucrative.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Y. Johnson and Kenneth Chang
item.media:credit: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

item.title: Five Essential Songs From Freddie Jackson: ‘You Are My Lady’ and More
item.description: A central figure in the Quiet Storm R&B of the 1980s, Jackson explored a tender and refined longing on tracks like “You Are My Lady” and “Jam Tonight.”
item.dc:creator: Niela Orr

item.title: Freddie Jackson, ‘You Are My Lady’ Singer That Topped R&B Charts, Dead at 69
item.description: With hits like “Rock Me Tonight (For Old Times Sake)” and “You Are My Lady,” he made slow jams feel like grand romance.
item.dc:creator: Mark Walker
item.media:description: Freddie Jackson performing in Indiana in 1986, the year he received two Grammy nominations.

item.title: Eva Marie Saint, Oscar Winner for ‘On the Waterfront,’ Is Dead at 102
item.description: A luminous beauty with dramatic depth, she brought a layered intensity to harrowing roles and seduced Cary Grant in the romantic thriller “North by Northwest.”
item.dc:creator: Aljean Harmetz
item.media:description: Eva Marie Saint and Cary Grant in Alfred Hitchcock’s “North by Northwest” in 1959. She said some of the easiest work in her entire professional life involved the many retakes required to film their kissing scenes.

item.title: ‘Sudden’ Sam McDowell, Ace Pitcher for the Cleveland Indians, Has Died
item.description: Known as “Sudden Sam,” he led the American League in strikeouts five times and posted a single-season high of 325 in 1965.
item.dc:creator: Richard Goldstein
item.media:description: Sam McDowell was named to the A.L. All-Star team six times.

item.title: An Influential Voice in the Climate Debate Has Died at 66
item.description: Joe Romm was a prolific writer who never hesitated to take on climate change deniers and the fossil-fuel industry — or even ostensible allies.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen

item.title: How a Painstaking Scholar Reinterpreted African History
item.description: In six major books, John Iliffe centered his research not on kings, dictators and guerrilla chiefs but rather on ordinary African citizens. He has died at 87.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter

item.title: Beef, Comedy, Sports and a Big Bad Bet. George Gillett Jr., Tycoon, Dies.
item.description: Over six decades, he owned TV stations, a meatpacking plant, the Globetrotters, the Montreal Canadiens and the Liverpool soccer club. It didn’t all end well.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir
item.media:description: In 2001, George Gillett Jr. paid an estimated $275 million for 80 percent of the Montreal Canadiens and 100 percent of their arena. In 2009, he sold the team, the arena and the entertainment division he had created for about $550 million.

item.title: Jim Bakker, TV Evangelist Felled by Fraud and Sex Scandals, Dies
item.description: With his wife, Tammy Faye, Mr. Bakker built a broadcasting juggernaut around the gospel of prosperity.
item.dc:creator: Clyde Haberman
item.media:description: Jim Bakker in 1987. The television ministry he founded with his first wife, Tammy Faye Bakker, brought in as much as $129 million annually before he was felled by a sex scandal.

item.title: Cheikh Hamidou Kane, Author of Seminal Anticolonial Novel, Dies at 98
item.description: The Senegalese writer was lauded as one of the founding fathers of African literature who subtly captured the shock of colonization from the perspective of the continent’s people.
item.dc:creator: Adam Nossiter
item.media:description: Cheikh Hamidou Kane in 2011. Mr. Kane subtly captured the shock of colonization from the perspective of the African people.

item.title: Jeffrey Archer, Novelist Whose Real Life Rivaled His Thrillers, Dies at 86
item.description: In a life of achievement and disgrace, he wrote best-selling novels with themes he knew intimately: ambition, self-promotion, misbehavior and scandal.
item.dc:creator: Alan Cowell
item.category: Stranger Than Fiction: Lives of the Twentieth-Century Novel (Book)
item.media:credit: Rick Eglinton/Toronto Star, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Jeffrey Archer’s latest book was scheduled for publication on Tuesday.

item.title: The City Leader Who Revived Central Park Dies at 85
item.description: Gordon J. Davis was New York City’s first Black parks commissioner and one of the most effective. He also led Lincoln Center.
item.dc:creator: Robin Pogrebin and Sam Roberts
item.media:credit: Benjamin Norman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Gordon J. Davis in 2016. “He woke up the parks department from what it was, which was terrible,” said Diane M. Coffey, former chief of staff to Mayor Edward I. Koch.

item.title: Ben Watson, a Cider Expert Known as Brother Apple, Has Died at 64.
item.description: Ben Watson, also known as Brother Apple, played a pivotal role in turning cider into a thriving slice of America’s craft-beverage movement. He has died at 64.
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Rosenwald

item.title: Dennis Hastert, Powerful Politician Disgraced by Child Sexual Abuse, Dies
item.description: The longest-serving Republican speaker of the House admitted in 2016 to abusing teenage boys decades earlier. He was 84.
item.dc:creator: Carl Hulse
item.media:description: Dennis Hastert on Capitol Hill in 2003. He was sentenced to 15 months in federal prison in April 2016.

item.title: Biljana Plavsic, a Former Bosnian Serb Political Leader, Has Died
item.description: Biljana Plavsic, a Bosnian Serb, pleaded guilty to one count of crimes against humanity. She later recanted and said she “would do the same again.”
item.dc:creator: Andrew Higgins
item.category: War Crimes, Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity
International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia
Human Rights and Human Rights Violations
item.media:description: Biljana Plavsic during her first appearance at the International Criminal Tribunal in The Hague in 2001.

item.title: Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio For Decades, Dies at 100
item.description: The actor played the role of the sweetly endearing mouse puppet, a character beloved by children all over the world — and, apparently, Ed Sullivan.
item.dc:creator: Kaja Andric
item.media:credit: Mario Notarangelo Mondadori Portfolio, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Mr. Mazzullo in the 1970s with Topo Gigio and the puppet’s designer, Maria Perego.

item.title: Overlooked No More: Eugenia Errázuriz, Who Opened Doors for Picasso
item.description: She moved from Chile to Paris, where she used her wealth to support Picasso, Stravinsky and other artists. World War II forced her to go home, where she ended her life.
item.dc:creator: Penelope Rowlands

item.title: Linda Asher, Who Widened The New Yorker’s Taste in Fiction, Dies at 93
item.description: She published new voices like Haruki Murakami at the magazine and translated stories and books by Milan Kundera and Balzac from French.
item.dc:creator: Richard Sandomir

item.title: Brooke Eby, Who Brought Humor and Awareness to A.L.S., Dies at 37
item.description: After her diagnosis in 2022, when she was only 33, she became a vocal, witty advocate for people confronting the disease.
item.dc:creator: Clay Risen
item.media:credit: Gesi Schilling for The New York Times
